The petitioners have filed this claim petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against the respondents for seeking compensation on account of death of one Smt.R.Pavithra D/o Rajappa Reddy and W/o P.Ranjith, in the Motor Vehicle Accident.
02.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioners is as under:
That on 01.08.2023 at about 05.00 a.m, the said R.Pavithra, her parents Rajappareddy and Vanajakshi, her in-laws N.Prabhakar Reddy and Sumithra and her mother-in-law's mother Pullamma, totally six of them left home from Govindashetty Palya to Kancheepuram for purchase of clothes in a SUV Mahindra Car bearing No.KA-51-MN-7587 which belongs to father of the deceased and he was driving the same.

While travelling, both father and father-in-law of the deceased were sitting in the front seat and four women were sitting in the back seat and the father of the deceased was driving the same slowly by observing all traffic rules from Krishnagiri to Dharmapuri National Highway Road, at about 05.55 a.m near Thimmapuram Government High School, Opp. Chinnaswamy's house, a private bus by name R.B.T (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.691/2024 Vanivil bearing No.TN-30-BL-6688 moving from Krishnagiri to Salem, driven by its driver in a high speed, rash and negligent manner violating all traffic rules
, came from behind and hit the back side of the car and the same got completely damaged.
Due to which the said R.Pavithra sustained severe head injuries and immediately after the accident she was shifted to Government Medical College hospital, Krishnagiri and

about 06.30 a.m the doctor who checked Ranjith P vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122971933/
2 said R.Pavithra and declared dead.

sentences.text:
The petitioner No.2 has spent Rs.2,00,000/-
towards hospital expenses, transportation of deadbody and funeral rites of the deceased.

Prior to the accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 25 years and was a BBA graduate from PES College, Bengaluru and was a distinction holder throughout her schooling and college and after marriage she was doing a part time job at home after completing her household work, as she was doing flower decoration work for the flower vendor nearby house and was paid Rs.300 to Rs.350 per day depending upon the work delivered by her, totaling to Rs.10,000/- p.m.
Out of which, she was supporting her parents by giving half the amount to them for their household expenses.

Due to untimely death of the deceased, the petitioner No.1 (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.691/2024 has lost his loving life partner, whose absence, he is unable to bear and which cannot be compensated by any means, petitioners No.2 and 3 have lost their loving daughter and petitioner No.4 has lost his adorable sister.
The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending private Bus and in this regard the Kaveripattinam Police have registered a case against driver of the offending bus.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the said offending vehicle,
are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- to the petitioners together with cost and interest.
03. Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.2 remained absent and hence, was placed exparte.
On service of notice, the respondent No.1 has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and has filed objections.

04. The respondent No.1 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioners and further denied age, income, occupation of deceased and manner of accident, involvement of the bus in the alleged accident, injuries sustained by the deceased, expenses incurred by the petitioners,
dependency of the petitioners with the deceased and admits that this (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.691/2024 respondent has issued the insurance policy in favour of respondent No.2 in respect of vehicle bearing No. TN-30-BL-6688 covering the risk of the said vehicle and the liability is according to terms and conditions of the policy.

The compensation claimed is exorbitant and hence, pray for dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.1.
05.

Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following Issues have been framed by my learned predecessor: -
ISSUES 01. Whether petitioners prove that they are the LRs/dependents of deceased Smt.R.Pavithra W/o P.Ranjith?

02. Whether petitioners prove that deceased Smt.R.Pavithra W/o P.Ranjith, was died in RTA arising out of the accident alleged to have been taken place on 01.08.2023 at about 5.55 a.m, on Krishnagiri to Dharmapuri NH Road, near Thimmapuram Govt.
High School, opposite Chinnaswami house, due to rash and negligent driving of Ranjith P vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122971933/

In order to prove their case, the petitioners No.1 and 3 got examined themselves as PW.1 and 2 and through them got marked 18 documents as Ex.P.1 to 18 and closed their side evidence.

07. By way of rebuttal, the respondent No.1 did not lead evidence inspite of sufficient opportunity has been given, hence respondent No.1 evidence is taken as nil and closed its side evidence.
08.
Heard both sides.
The counsels for the petitioners and respondent No.1 have filed written arguments.

09. My findings on the aforesaid Issues are as under:-
Issue No.1 Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.2 In the Affirmative Issue No.3 Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.4 As per final order for the following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1:-
Petitioners No.1 and 3 have filed affidavit stating that, they are the husband and mother, petitioner No.2 is the father and petitioner No.4 is the younger brother of the deceased.

To prove the said facts, they have produced Death certificate of (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.691/2024 deceased, original copies of SSLC, first and second year PUC marks cards, Marriage invitation card and two photographs of deceased, original copy of Aadhaar card of deceased and Notarized copy of driving licence of petitioner No.2 as per Ex.P.6 to 9, 12, 16, 17 and 18 which shows that the petitioners are the husband and parents of the deceased.
But the petitioner No.4 is major brother of the deceased and he has his own source of income.
Hence, this tribunal is of the considered opinion that petitioner No.4 is not the dependent on the deceased.
There is no dispute in their cross-examination regarding relationship of the petitioners No.1 to 3 with the deceased.
So, on perusal of these documents, it is true that the petitioners No.1 to 3 are the legal representatives and dependents on the deceased.
Accordingly, this Issue is answered partly in the affirmative.

sentences.text: Issue No.2:- The petitioners No.1 and 3
got themselves examined as PW.1 and 2 and they have given evidence in the form of the affidavit and they have reiterated the petition averments therein.

Though, they have been elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.1 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioners that due to rash and negligent driving of the offending Bus (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.691/2024 by its driver, the deceased has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident and later died.
On perusal of the documents, Ex.P.1 is Post mortem report of deceased R.Pavithra shows the cause of death is due to shock and hemorrhage due to multiple injuries.

Ex.P.2 is Final report shows after completion of investigation the Investigation Officer has filed final report against driver of the offending Bus for the offences punishable U/s 279,
337, 304(A) of IPC.
Ex.P.2A is translation copy of final report.

Ex.P.3 is Spot Mahazar with Sketch showing the place of accident on Krishnagiri - Dharmapuri NH Road, near Thimmapuram Government High School, Opp. Chinnaswamy's house and agriculture cultural land, which is not disputed.
Ex.P.3A is translation copy of Spot Mahazar and Sketch.
Ex.P.4 is IMV report shows involvement of offending bus in the accident and damages caused to its front and left hand side.
Ex.P.5 is Inquest Panchanama of deceased R.Pavithra.
Ex.P.5A is translation copy of Inquest Panchanama.
Ex.P.13 is the FIR registered at Kaveripattinam Police against driver of the offending bus.
Ex.P.13A is translation copy of FIR.
Ex.P.14 is Complaint which shows that due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending bus, the accident took place and (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.691/2024 deceased sustained injuries.
Ex.P.14A is translation copy of Complaint.

The oral and documentary evidence adduced by the petitioners clearly goes to show that the accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of offending bus and deceased sustained injuries and later died.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.3:- This Issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the death of the deceased R.Pavithra, who died in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

The PW.1 and PW.2 in their evidence and pleadings have stated that prior to accident deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 25 years and was a BBA graduate and was a distinction holder and after marriage she was doing a part time job at home after completing her household work, as she was doing flower decoration work for the flower vendor nearby house and was paid Rs.300 to Rs.350 per day depending upon the work delivered by her, totaling to Rs.10,000/- p.m and they have spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards hospital expenses, transportation of deadbody and funeral rites of the deceased.
Due to untimely death of the deceased, the petitioners are put to great (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.691/2024 financial loss, loss of love and affection and mental agony.
13. It is the duty of the petitioners to prove age of the deceased as on the date of accident.
The petitioners have not produced any birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card of the deceased to show the exact date of birth of the deceased.
However, they have produced Ex.P.7 SSLC marks card and Ex.P.17 Aadhaar card of deceased.

Even though said documents are not authenticated documents for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of other evidence,
said documents can be relied upon and according to which the date of birth of the deceased is Ranjith P vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122971933/

sentences.text: The alleged accident occurred on 01.08.2023 and hence it appears that as on the date of accident the age of the deceased is 25 years.

Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 25 years and as per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 15 to 25 years is "18".

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So far as avocation and income of deceased is concerned, the petitioners have not placed any materials before the tribunal.

Therefore, in the absence of evidence regarding his avocation and income, this tribunal has to go by the Lok-Adalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2023 to be taken as Rs.16,000/- p.m.

Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the deceased is at Rs.16,000/- and it is multiplied by 12.
15.
In the case on hand, undoubtedly the petitioner No.1 is the husband and petitioners No.2 and 3 are the parents of the deceased and they are the dependents on the earnings of the deceased.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & others case, the future prospects or additional income should be added to monthly income of the deceased.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since deceased was aged 25 years at the time of accident and she comes in the age group of below 40 years and was self employee, 40% income should be added to the monthly income towards future prospects which would be result in the income to be (16,000 + 6,400) = Rs.22,400/-.

Therefore, considering the (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.691/2024 materials available on record, this tribunal is of the opinion that since there are three dependents, it is appropriate to deduct 1/3rd of the income towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and then his monthly income would be (Rs.22,400 - Rs.7,467) =
Rs.14,933/-.
The income of the deceased for the purpose of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.14,933/-.
As the deceased was aged about 25 years, the multiplier of 18 would have to be applied.

Consequently the claimants would be entitled for a sum of (Rs.14,933 x 12 x 18)
Rs.32,25,528/- is awarded towards loss of dependency.

16. In view of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi & Others case, in respect to loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses, the aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every 3 years.

sentences.text:
Accordingly, in the head of loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses,
10% is enhanced for period of every 3 years.
17. The claimant No.1 is the husband and claimants No.2 and 3 are the parents of the deceased.

Therefore, petitioners No.1 to 3 are entitled for Rs.48,400/- each towards loss of spousal (SCCH-3)
14 M.V.C.No.691/2024 consortium and filial consortium and petitioners are also entitled for Rs.18,150/- each towards loss of estate and funeral expenses and transportation of dead body.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and noticing the number of dependents and 1/3rd of the income taken into consideration towards the personal and living expenses of the deceased, this Tribunal has placed reliance on ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a Ranjith P vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122971933/

19. Regarding liability:- Despite sufficient opportunity, the respondent No.2 remained absent and was placed exparte.
On service of notice, the respondent No.1 has appeared and filed objections and contested the matter, but not lead evidence to disprove the case of the petitioners and to prove its contention.
On the date of accident policy was in force.
Hence, respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay above said compensation amount.
Respondent No.1 Insurance Company is directed to deposit above said compensation amount within two months from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.3 partly in affirmative.
20. Issue No.4:
In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER The petition filed by the petitioners U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.34,07,028/- (Rupees Thirty four lakhs seven thousand and twenty eight only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the petitioners No.1 to 3 are entitled to get release 70% each of the award through E-payment directly to their account by obtaining the bank account details on proper identification without any further proceedings and remaining 30% each shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.
